title: Marker scan and last-match tracker
statement: Let $P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The length of the prefix before the last true entry in the word $(P(0),\ldots,P(n-1))$, when such an entry exists, and no value otherwise, is the last index below $n$ at which $P$ is true, or is undefined if there is no such index.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean-valued predicate on the natural numbers
replaced: For every predicate $P$ and bound $n$, mapping the length over the last-true split of the flag word of $P$ on indices $0,\dots,n-1$ yields exactly the tracker's last matching index below $n$.
